transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I keep rechecking and fixing how I look before I go out or get on camera, and it’s starting to make me late and stressed all the time. It's just gotten really hard to manage lately, so my sister suggested I come talk to someone.

Do you feel driven by unwanted thoughts that something is wrong with your appearance and have to check or fix it to relieve anxiety, or is it more that you prefer things to look just right because you’re very perfectionistic in general?

It’s definitely the first one, because I get these constant, unwanted thoughts that specific things are wrong with my face, like my jaw looking crooked or my skin looking bad. I end up stuck in front of the mirror adjusting my hair, changing shirts, and taking test selfies over and over just to feel "less ugly" and relieve that anxiety. It’s not really about being a general perfectionist, it's just about trying to fix those specific things so I can leave the house.

Are these unwanted thoughts and repeated checking almost entirely about your appearance, or do you also have other obsessions or rituals not related to how you look, like contamination, checking, counting, or arranging things?

It is almost entirely about my appearance, like worrying about my jaw looking crooked, my skin, or my hair and clothes. I don't have any other rituals or obsessions like worrying about germs, counting, or arranging things. It's really just focused on how I look.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports persistent preoccupation with perceived defects in appearance, experienced as intrusive and unwanted, along with repetitive appearance-related behaviors such as mirror checking, changing clothes, adjusting hair, and repeated test selfies to reduce anxiety. The symptoms are narrowly focused on appearance rather than broader obsessive-compulsive themes, supporting body dysmorphic disorder/somatic symptom-related hypochondriacal disorder coding under ICD-10 F45.2.
